chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from `Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu `Abd Allah (peace be upon him) saying:

He wills, He intends, He dislikes, and He is pleased. He wills that nothing should exist except with His Knowledge, and He intends similar to that. He dislikes it to be said of Him: 'The third of three,' and He is pleased with His servants' disbelief.
ai.seo_question: What are the four divine attributes of Will, Intention, Dislike, and Pleasure in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to articulate the distinct nuances of divine attributes, distinguishing between God's universal Will (Shawq) which encompasses all existence through His Knowledge, and His specific Intention (Irada) and Pleasure (Rida). It highlights His dislike of the Trinitarian concept of being a 'third of three' while affirming His pleasure with the disbelief of His servants, a key point in Shia theological debates regarding divine decree and human agency.
